method.text: Two linear models per sensor. The cause model predicts it from the operating conditions only (wind speed, power, rotor speed, outside temperature, with 3- and 12-hour averages for thermal lag), so a failing part cannot hide behind neighbouring sensors that heat up with it. The peer model predicts it from its 5 best-correlated sensors and checks the sensor itself. Fitted on the first 85% of the training year, threshold = 99th percentile of the absolute residual on the rest, then the case's prediction window is watched. An episode is 30 minutes above the threshold. A sensor warns when its episodes run above its own normal rate: a CUSUM adds up each day's evidence for a 4-fold rate and warns at Wald's boundary for a 0.1% false-alarm and 10% missed-alarm risk, so a steady trickle of episodes counts as much as a burst. A component (gearbox, generator, transformer, ...) warns when 1 of its sensors warn within 3 days; a sensor that leaves its near-duplicate twin, or fails the quality checks, does not count. The first component warning is the turbine alarm.
